problem.text: A three-dimensional rectangular box with dimensions $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ has faces whose surface areas are $24$, $24$, $48$, $48$, $72$, and $72$ square units. What is $X+Y+Z$?

steps.title: Where to start: each face uses two of the edges
steps.body:
A box has three pairs of opposite faces, and opposite faces are equal. That is why the six areas come in pairs. Each face is a rectangle made from two of the three edges, so we can name the faces so that
$$XY = 24, \quad YZ = 48, \quad ZX = 72.$$

your_turn.prompt: Each edge letter shows up in how many of the three products $XY$, $YZ$, $ZX$?
your_turn.answer: Two. For example, $X$ is in $XY$ and in $ZX$.

steps.title: Multiply all three equations
steps.body:
Since each letter appears exactly twice, multiplying the three products gives $X^2Y^2Z^2$, the square of $XYZ$. Factor the numbers into primes to take the square root easily.
$$(XYZ)^2 = 24 \cdot 48 \cdot 72 = 2^{10} \cdot 3^4$$

steps.title: Divide to get each edge
steps.body: Now divide $XYZ$ by one face area to get the edge that face does not use. For example, $YZ = 48$ leaves out $X$, so $X = 288 \div 48$.

your_turn.prompt: Which edge is left out of the face with area $24$, and how long is it?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The edges are $X = 288 \div 48 = 6$, $Y = 288 \div 72 = 4$, and $Z = 12$. Check: $6 \cdot 4 = 24$, $4 \cdot 12 = 48$, $6 \cdot 12 = 72$. So $X + Y + Z = 6 + 4 + 12 = 22$. The answer is **(B)**.

verification.verifier_notes: Passed adversarial verifier on first review.
